chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If you have a stay in Medina for three days, you should fast on the first day, Wednesday, and pray on the night of Wednesday at the pillar of Abu Lubabah, which is the pillar of repentance to which he tied himself until his excuse descended from the sky. You should sit at it on Wednesday, then come on the night of Thursday that follows, from the side facing the standing place of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), for your night and your day, and fast on Thursday. Then come to the pillar that faces the standing place of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and his prayer place on the night of Friday, so you pray at it for your night and your day, and fast on Friday. And if you can, do not speak anything during these days except what you must, do not leave the mosque except for a need, and do not sleep during the night or the day; then do so, for that is among that which is counted as merit.
Then praise God on Friday, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and ask for your need.

And let what you say be: 'O God, whatever need I have of You, whether I began seeking and requesting it or did not begin, whether I asked You for it or did not ask You for it, I turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, the Prophet of Mercy, peace be upon him and his family, for the fulfillment of my needs, small and large. For You are worthy that your need be fulfilled, if God wills.'

As for the fasting of the vow, it is of three types: One is that he vows to fast for God Almighty for a month or a specified number of days, so that fasting becomes obligatory upon him, and it is not permissible for him to fast while traveling. The second is that he vows the fasting of a specific day, and that day coincides with him being a traveler, so its ruling is the ruling of the first in that it is not permissible for him to fast it while traveling. The third is that he specifies the fasting of a specific day and stipulates upon himself that he fast it while traveling and while resident, and at that time it becomes obligatory upon him to fast that day while traveling just as it is obligatory upon him while resident. And that which indicates the first category is what they narrated:

key_terms.أُسْطُوَانَةُ التَّوْبَةِ: Pillar of Repentance (a specific historical pillar in Medina)
key_terms.الْحَضَر: Residence/Staying in one's home city (opposite of travel)
key_terms.صَوْمُ النَّذْرِ: Fasting of the vow (voluntary fasting made obligatory by a vow)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended acts of worship in Medina and the legal rulings for fasting vows in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the spiritual etiquette of visiting Medina, emphasizing silence and continuous worship at the 'Pillar of Repentance' (Ustuwana Abu Lubabah) to seek divine acceptance. It transitions into a nuanced juristic analysis of *nadhr* (vows), clarifying whether fasting obligations persist during travel based on the specificity of the vow's conditions. This reflects the Shia scholarly focus on aligning personal devotion with legal flexibility in varying circumstances.
